title: Szczęśliwego Nowego Roku!
focus: New Year’s Eve: telling the time, resolutions, aspect and the conditional

patterns.speaker: Gender follows the speaker
patterns.numbers: Numbers and the case of the noun

lines.speaker: Marek
lines.pl: Za|za pięć dwunasta|dwunasta! Gdzie są kieliszki|kieliszki?
lines.en: Five to midnight! Where are the glasses?

lines.speaker: Ania
lines.pl: Na stole|stole, obok szampana|szampana. Tomek, otworzysz|otworzysz butelkę|butelke?
lines.en: On the table, next to the champagne. Tomek, will you open the bottle?

lines.speaker: Tomek
lines.pl: Już się robi. Ale najpierw powiedzcie|powiedzcie: jakie macie postanowienia|postanowienia noworoczne|noworoczne?
lines.en: Coming right up. But first, tell me: what are your New Year’s resolutions?

lines.speaker: Marek
lines.pl: Od jutra|jutra będę biegał|biegal trzy razy|razy w tygodniu.
lines.en: From tomorrow I’m going to run three times a week.

lines.speaker: Ania
lines.pl: Mówiłeś|mowiles to samo w zeszłym roku. Wytrzymałeś|wytrzymales dwa tygodnie|tygodnie.
lines.en: You said the same thing last year. You lasted two weeks.

lines.speaker: Marek
lines.pl: Dlatego w tym roku kupiłem|kupilem sobie|sobie nowe buty. A ty, Aniu|aniu?
lines.en: That’s why this year I’ve bought myself new shoes. And you, Ania?

lines.speaker: Ania
lines.pl: Chciałabym|chcialabym wreszcie nauczyć|nauczyc się prowadzić samochód. Gdybym|gdybym zdała|zdala egzamin, pojechalibyśmy|pojechalibysmy w lecie|lecie nad morze|morze.
lines.en: I’d like to finally learn to drive. If I passed the test, we could drive to the seaside in the summer.

lines.speaker: Wszyscy
lines.pl: Dziesięć, dziewięć, osiem… trzy, dwa, jeden! Szczęśliwego|szczesliwego Nowego|nowego Roku|roku!
lines.en: Ten, nine, eight… three, two, one! Happy New Year!

lines.speaker: Tomek
lines.en: All the best for the year ahead!

za.why: Telling the time before the hour: za + minutes + the hour as a feminine ordinal in the nominative: za pięć dwunasta, “five to twelve.” After the hour it’s po + locative: pięć po dwunastej.

parts: fem. sg., agreeing with an understood godzina
dwunasta.why: Clock times are ordinal numbers agreeing with an understood godzina, which is feminine: (godzina) dwunasta, “twelve o’clock.”

kieliszki.why: A kieliszek is a stemmed glass; a szklanka is a tumbler. The e is fleeting: kieliszek, kieliszki.

stole.why: Na + locative. Two changes: ó becomes o when the syllable opens, and ł becomes l before -e: stół → na stole.

szampana.why: Obok + genitive: obok szampana, “next to the champagne.”

otworzysz.why: A question in the perfective future works as a friendly request: otworzysz?, “will you open it?”

powiedzcie.why: Powiedzieć has an irregular imperative: powiedz to one person, powiedzcie to several. Tomek is asking everyone.

postanowienia.why: Postanowienie, “resolution”, is the verbal noun of postanowić, “to decide.”

noworoczne.why: A compound adjective built from nowy rok. The k of rok changes to cz before the suffix -n-, as in roczny, “annual.”

jutra.why: Od + genitive, “from, starting”: od jutra, “from tomorrow.” Jutro is used as a noun here.

biegal.tags: verb · imperfective · l-participle · masculine (future with będę)
biegal.why: Będę biegał is the imperfective future with the l-participle. Biegać is the indeterminate “run” (regularly, for exercise); biec is running in one direction.

razy.why: Raz has an unusual genitive plural, razy, the same as its nominative plural: dwa razy, pięć razy. Trzy razy w tygodniu means “three times a week.”

mowiles.tags: verb · imperfective · past · 2nd person singular · masculine
mowiles.why: Imperfective: Ania isn’t reporting one statement but what he kept saying. Masculine because she’s talking to Marek.

wytrzymales.tags: verb · perfective · past · 2nd person singular · masculine
wytrzymales.why: Perfective: he held out for two weeks, and that was the end of it. Wy- here means “all the way through.”

parts: stem tygodń- (ń spelled ni before a vowel)
tygodnie.why: Duration in the accusative with no preposition: dwa tygodnie, “(for) two weeks.” With 2–4, the ordinary plural.

kupilem.tags: verb · perfective · past · 1st person singular · masculine
kupilem.why: Perfective: the shoes are bought. Masculine because Marek is speaking.

sobie.why: Sobie is the dative of the reflexive pronoun. Kupiłem sobie means “I bought (for) myself.” With a plural subject it can also mean “each other”: składamy sobie życzenia.

aniu.why: Diminutive names in -ia take -u in the vocative: Ania → Aniu, Kasia → Kasiu. Compare Krystyna → Krystyno.

chcialabym.tags: verb · imperfective · conditional · 1st person singular · feminine
chcialabym.why: The conditional for a wish: chciałabym, “I’d like.” Feminine because Ania is speaking.

nauczyc.why: Uczyć się is “to study”; the perfective nauczyć się is “to learn”, with success. It takes an infinitive or the genitive: nauczyć się prowadzić, nauczyć się polskiego.

gdybym.why: The person marker attaches to gdyby, and the verb stays a bare past form: gdybym zdała, “if I passed.”

zdala.why: Zdać egzamin means “to pass an exam.” The imperfective zdawać egzamin means only “to take an exam.” This is a classic aspect trap for learners.

pojechalibysmy.tags: verb · perfective · conditional · 1st person plural · virile
pojechalibysmy.why: Virile because the group includes men. The structure is the same as poszlibyśmy in Plany na sobotę, with jechać for travel by vehicle.

you.f: With a mixed group: pojechalibyśmy. Only women: pojechałybyśmy.

parts: t → ć before loc. -e, spelled ci
lecie.why: W lecie, “in summer”: lato in the locative, with a → e and t → ć. Latem means the same.

morze.tags: noun · neuter · accusative singular (same as nominative)
morze.why: Nad + accusative for going to the seaside or a lake: jechać nad morze. Being there takes the instrumental: nad morzem.

szczesliwego.why: Szczęśliwego Nowego Roku!, “Happy New Year!”: genitive after an understood życzę, like Wesołych Świąt.

nowego.why: Agrees with Roku. In the name of the holiday both words are capitalised: Nowy Rok.

roku.why: Genitive singular of rok, the head of the wish.

siego.why: Do siego roku is a fixed New Year wish, roughly “(may you live) to this coming year.” Siego is the genitive of an Old Polish pronoun meaning “this” that survives only in this phrase.

exercises.explain: Za + minutes + the hour as a feminine ordinal: za dziesięć ósma.

exercises.prompt: “I passed my driving test!” (zdać): ___ egzamin na prawo jazdy!

explain.m: Perfective zdać, so you passed: Zda + ł + e + m. Zdawałem would only mean you took it.
explain.f: Perfective zdać, so you passed: Zda + ł + a + m. Zdawałam would only mean you took it.

exercises.hint: Zdawać means “to take an exam.” Which verb means you passed? Then check the learner setting.

exercises.prompt: Two women: “We would go to the mountains”: ___ w góry.
exercises.explain: No men in the group, so the non-virile ending -y, and ł stays ł: pojechałybyśmy.
exercises.hint: Compare pojechalibyśmy. What changes when there are no men?

exercises.explain: Like stół → na stole: ó → o and ł → l before -e: na dole.

exercises.prompt: Wish someone good health (dobre zdrowie): Dużo ___ zdrowia!
exercises.explain: Wishes take the genitive: dobrego zdrowia.
